The ongoing crisis in Gaza has caused widespread destruction of infrastructure, services, and livelihoods.Recovery and reconstruction efforts are underway, yet women remain underrepresented in decision-making and leadership roles, despite being disproportionately affected by the crisis. Women—particularly female-headed households, young women, and women with disabilities—face compounded barriers to accessing resources, influencing recovery planning, and benefiting fromreconstruction processes. Atthe same time, they are key agents of change, leading community coping mechanisms, informal economies, and social support systems.
Problem analysis:
The project addresses main problem of Repeated forced displacement, discriminatory gender <(>&<)> socio-culturalnorms, rise in GBV risks and harmful practices, Limited participation, decision-making, and engagement of women in recovery and reconstruction processes. The project also addresses the lack of women's voice, agency, leadership and effective participation of localwomen/ young women and women-led organizations in decision-making bodies and processes related to humanitarian response, early recovery, reconstruction, social cohesion, and local peacebuilding. It responds to protection risks; access barriers <(>&<)> urgent needs of women/girls identified in needs assessment/ gender analysis conducted by WAC on 23-27/7/2025.

participating-org.narrative: The Womens Affairs Centre in Gaza focuses on research and training to promote the equal rights of women in Palestinian society. Itsgoal is to empower women politically, economically and socially and to promote gender awareness in Palestinian society. WAC does this through a program of research, training and lobby to overcome obstacles to the equality of men and women, to analyse and develop tools and strategies for overcoming them. WAC is also involved in activities such as training women to set up and improve small enterprises, in how to use cameras for making videos and films, and in writing and computer skills. The research program is linked to its activities on the themes of child marriages, violence against women and womens rights. WAC has been working in Gaza since 1991 andOxfam Novib has been supporting it since 1992.
